source: Zhang et al. (2025) Reasoning Models Know When They are Right: Probing Hidden States for Self-Verification (in-distribution)
finding: A small probe on hidden states at intermediate-answer positions in long chain-of-thought predicts whether that answer is correct. This is a machine version of a graded 'am I close' signal.
numbers: R1-Distill-Llama-8B in-distribution accuracy: GSM8K 0.77, MATH 0.80, AIME 0.85, KnowLogic 0.62. ECE 0.05 GSM8K, 0.03 MATH, 0.10 AIME, 0.07 KnowLogic. Best ECE 0.01 (Qwen-32B, GSM8K); worst 0.13 (QwQ-32B, MATH). Six reasoning models plus Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct as control.
limits: Abstract claims ECE under 0.1, but Table 1 has cells at 0.10, 0.13, 0.14. Chunk labels came from Gemini 2.0 Flash, not humans. Training sets capped at 1,000 examples.
agent_relevance: Needs hidden states, so not usable with a closed API model. Shows correctness is readable mid-solution, which supports a graded rather than hard stop trigger.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) Reasoning Models Know When They are Right: Probing Hidden States for Self-Verification (transfer and short-CoT control)
finding: The probe transfers between math sets but poorly to harder or different domains. On a non-reasoning model it works much worse, so the signal seems learned in long-CoT training.
numbers: R1-Distill-Llama-8B AUC/ECE: GSM8K->MATH 0.80/0.08; MATH->GSM8K 0.83/0.04; GSM8K->AIME 0.69/0.25; MATH->AIME 0.76/0.28; KnowLogic->AIME 0.81/0.31. Short-CoT Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct probe 'much worse' (exact values only in a figure).
limits: Calibration breaks out of distribution (ECE up to 0.31). Origin of the ability not explained.
agent_relevance: A monitor must be recalibrated per task family. Do not reuse one threshold across suites.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) Reasoning Models Know When They are Right: Probing Hidden States for Self-Verification (look-ahead and early exit)
finding: Correctness can be predicted before the answer is fully written, and a confidence-based exit saves tokens at near equal accuracy.
numbers: MATH, R1-Distill-Llama-8B: peak probe accuracy 79%; at 10%, 50%, 95% of the way into the answer it is 14, 10, 5 points lower. Early exit at threshold 0.85: 88.2% accuracy, about 24% fewer tokens; threshold 0.9: 88.6% (equals no exit), about 19% fewer. Static exit at similar tokens: about 82.5%.
limits: Early-exit tested on one model and one dataset (MATH, 10K token cap). Probe is trained on that model's own traces.
agent_relevance: Direct analogue of a 'close to solution, stop and answer' rule. A confidence stop beat a fixed-length stop by up to 5 points here.

source: Kadavath et al. (2022) Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
finding: Large models can judge whether their own sampled answer is true (P(True)) and can predict before answering whether they know (P(IK)). This is the machine version of a feeling-of-knowing or warmth judgment.
numbers: Models 800M, 3B, 12B, 52B. P(IK) 52B AUROC trained on TriviaQA only: Python function synthesis 0.928, LAMBADA 0.864 (Brier 0.151), GSM8K 0.687 (Brier 0.164). AUROC rises with model size. Training on all tasks improves every transfer.
limits: Zero-shot P(True) is poorly calibrated and sits near 50%; calibration needs few-shot and showing other samples. Judging own samples is harder than judging a third party's options. Pre-RLHF models only. Row-to-task mapping of Table 1 read from a text dump, so the per-task AUROCs are approximate.
agent_relevance: Self-judgment of progress works only when calibrated against held-out data and with comparison samples. Supports G2/G5: do not trust a bare self-rating.

source: Huang et al. (2023) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Models cannot tell whether their reasoning is right. With oracle labels, self-correction helps; without them it often hurts. So a self-reported 'not there yet' is unreliable.
numbers: GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 -> 75.1 -> 74.7 over two rounds; CommonSenseQA 75.8 -> 38.1 -> 41.8. GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 -> 91.5 -> 89.0; HotpotQA 49.0 -> 49.0 -> 43.0. Llama-2 GSM8K 62.0 -> 43.5 -> 36.5. With oracle labels GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 -> 84.3, GPT-4 HotpotQA 49.0 -> 59.0.
limits: Generic 'review your answer' prompts; later work shows better scaffolds can help. Older models (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Llama-2).
agent_relevance: Backs G2 and G3: a progress or stuck trigger must come from code-checked output, not the model's own opinion.

source: Chen et al. (2024) Do NOT Think That Much for 2+3=? On the Overthinking of o1-Like LLMs
finding: Reasoning models fail to notice they already solved the problem and keep going. The first solution is usually right and most tokens come after it.
numbers: '2+3': o1-like models used 1,953% more tokens than conventional ones; QwQ produced 13 solutions in 901 tokens, outcome efficiency 4.3%. First solution correct in over 92% of cases; first round under 60% of tokens. Best mitigation SimPO+FCS+Reflection: MATH500 93.0% -> 92.8%, tokens 2407.9 -> 1330.7 (-44.7%); GSM8K 94.8 -> 96.0, -46.1%; AIME24 46.7 -> 43.3, -45.6%.
limits: Only QwQ-32B-Preview and DeepSeek-R1 as o1-like; mitigation needs training. Intro text and Table 4 disagree on which dataset got 48.6%.
agent_relevance: The reverse of progress monitoring: the model has no 'done' signal. A code-side rule such as 'stop after a check passes' addresses it.

source: Wang et al. (2025) Thoughts Are All Over the Place: On the Underthinking of o1-Like LLMs
finding: Opposite failure: models abandon promising lines too early and switch thoughts without finishing. Incorrect answers show 225% more tokens and 418% more thought switches.
numbers: Over 70% of incorrect responses contain at least one correct thought. AIME24 DeepSeek-R1-671B: accuracy 73.3, underthinking score 37.0; QwQ 46.7 / 65.0. A thought-switch penalty (Tip) on QwQ AIME24: Pass@1 38.3 -> 44.1, switches 16.1 -> 13.9; GPQA switches 21.1 -> 7.3, 57.6 -> 59.1. R1-671B AIME24 73.8 -> 74.8. QwQ+SC+Tip 16 samples: 53.9 vs SC alone 44.6.
limits: Correct-thought judgments come from an LLM assessor at about 82% accuracy (90 AIME items). Decoding penalty is a no-training fix but needs logit access.
agent_relevance: A progress rule must separate 'no progress, switch' from 'progress, stay'. Penalising early switching helped, which argues for a graded, not hair-trigger, trigger.

source: Shojaee et al. (2025) The Illusion of Thinking
finding: On puzzles, thinking effort rises with complexity and then falls just before accuracy collapses. On easy items correct answers come early and the model keeps exploring; at high complexity it fixates on an early wrong attempt.
numbers: Tower of Hanoi collapse at N=7-8 (about 100-200 moves); River Crossing collapse from N=3 (valid moves only to move 4); Checker Jumping at N=4; Blocks World R1 at N=4 greedy, N=30 with sampling. 25 samples per model per level. Giving the solution algorithm did not move the collapse point.
limits: Methods contested by critics (token limits, puzzle design). Read only the first 100,000 characters of the page.
agent_relevance: Models show no usable sense of 'I am failing'. They spend less effort exactly when nearing failure, so a code-side no-progress rule is needed.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts
finding: A state-value prompt asks the model to rate each partial solution sure / maybe / impossible. This is a machine progress monitor inside a search loop, and it gives large gains.
numbers: Game of 24: IO 7.3%, CoT 4.0%, CoT-SC k=100 9.0%, ToT b=1 45%, ToT b=5 74%. About 60% of CoT samples failed after the first step. Mini crosswords game success: IO 0, CoT 1, ToT 20, ToT minus pruning 5, ToT minus backtracking 5; word-level 60 vs 41.5 without pruning.
limits: Evaluator wrongly marks rare words impossible in solvable games; authors say better pruning heuristics are critical. GPT-4 only.
agent_relevance: Close to 'warmth' as a pruning signal. Shows the value of a graded state score, and its false-negative risk when it prunes true paths.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion
finding: A code rule triggers reflection when the agent is stuck: same action and same response for more than 3 cycles, or more than 30 actions in the episode. This is a hard no-progress trigger in a live LLM agent loop.
numbers: AlfWorld 134 tasks: ReAct+Reflexion solved 130 of 134, +22% absolute over baselines in 12 steps; ReAct alone plateaus between trials 6 and 7. HotPotQA ReAct gpt-4 0.39 -> 0.51; CoT(GT) gpt-4 0.68 -> 0.80. HumanEval pass@1 91.0 vs 80.1 prior.
limits: Thresholds (3 repeats, 30 actions) were set by hand with no ablation shown. Retry needs an environment reset and a memory of at most 3 reflections.
agent_relevance: Closest published precedent for our code-set no-progress rule. Our counts should be tuned on our own logs, not copied.

source: Answer convergence as a signal for early stopping in reasoning (2025; authors not extracted)
finding: Models usually reach their final answer well before the reasoning ends. Watching for repeated identical intermediate answers is a cheap progress signal.
numbers: Five open models. Abstract: convergence after about 60% of steps. Convergence point near 0.0 for NQ, about 0.8 for GSM8K/MATH-500, about 0.9 for GPQA and AIME24. Answer consistency (k=10 matching chunks): over 40% fewer tokens on NQ. Learn-to-Stop GSM8K QwQ 755.1 -> 418.9 tokens with 0.2% accuracy drop; GPQA 39.2% fewer tokens, accuracy 24.2 vs 25.3.
limits: Late stop is the main error: on GPQA R1-Qwen-32B 63.6% of stops were late. Gains shrink on hard tasks (convergence at 0.9).
agent_relevance: A count-based convergence rule (same answer k times) is code-checkable and fits our design. Savings shrink as difficulty rises.

source: Dynamic Early Exit in Reasoning Models, DEER (2025; authors not extracted)
finding: At each 'Wait' point the model is made to write a trial answer; if the geometric mean token confidence passes 0.95, stop. Cuts length and often raises accuracy.
numbers: 11 reasoning models, 10 benchmarks. Accuracy and length: R1-Distill-Qwen-7B 64.2 -> 69.2 (38.5% shorter); Qwen3-14B 82.8 -> 83.7 (42.9% shorter); QwQ-32B 82.6 -> 84.0 (19.1% shorter). AIME24 Qwen3-14B 70.0 -> 76.7. Failures: GPQA Qwen3-14B 60.1 -> 57.6; GSM8K QwQ 96.7 -> 96.3.
limits: Needs token log-probabilities. Threshold 0.95 fixed. Abstract range (19.1-80.1% shorter) differs from main table.
agent_relevance: Trial-answer probing at natural pause points is a model-side warmth reading that code can threshold.

source: Deep Think with Confidence, DeepConf (2025; authors not extracted)
finding: Sliding-window token confidence signals when a reasoning trace is going wrong; low-confidence traces are stopped or dropped.
numbers: GPT-OSS-120B AIME25: Pass@1 91.8%, majority@512 97.0%, DeepConf@512 99.9%. Online DeepConf-low cut tokens 43-79%; DeepSeek-8B AIME24 tokens -77.9% with accuracy 86.7 -> 92.5; GPT-OSS-120B AIME25 -84.7%. Window 2,048 tokens; 4,096 traces per problem.
limits: Confidently wrong traces slip through. Aggressive filtering hurt in 8 of 20 offline settings (-0.31 to -4.69 pp); DeepConf-low lost 4.4 pp on Qwen3-8B AIME25. Head-based confidence correlates weakly with correctness.
agent_relevance: Confidence is a graded progress signal usable to prune parallel attempts; matches G11/G12. Needs logprobs.

source: Cao et al. (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: A harness reads the model's feeling-of-knowing (before solving) and judgment-of-learning (after each attempt), thresholds them in code, and decides trust, retry with compact feedback, or aggregate. Built on Nelson-Narens monitoring and control.
numbers: Claude Sonnet-4.6 pooled 48.3 -> 56.9 (+8.6) over 1,859 items, avg 2.4 attempts, $0.78 per question. HLE-Verified 48.0 -> 60.0; LiveCodeBench v6 74.3 -> 84.3 (Hard 55.0 -> 74.6, Easy 95.4 -> 94.7); R-Bench-V 36.1 -> 41.1. Beats Self-Refine 52.4, Budget Forcing 51.5, Verifier Reranking 49.8, Aggregator 53.7 (single pass 48.3).
limits: Preprint, one base model for gains. Of 9 models tested only Opus-4.6 besides Sonnet reached 'Adequate Metacognition'. Hand-tuned rule 42.0 vs 47.0 for the learned SVM on a 100-item subset.
agent_relevance: Best modern evidence that code-thresholded self-ratings pay when ratings are calibrated. Warns that most models fail the calibration test.

source: Cao et al. (2026) Metacognitive Harness (diagnosis and ablations)
finding: Self-rated confidence must be diagnosed per model before use. Within-problem rating moves very little, so it cannot track progress through a solve, only separate problems.
numbers: Pass thresholds AUROC >= 0.60 and ECE <= 0.15. GPT-OSS JOL AUROC 0.87 but raw ECE 0.41, joint ECE 0.06 after SVM. Within-problem JOL std median 0.048 vs 0.270 across problems (about 5.6x). Ablation (100 items, pass@1 44.0): full 47.0; no FOK 45.0; no JOL 42.0; no SVM 42.0; random retry same K 45.7. Confidence bands pass@1 -> harness: low 0.16 -> 0.42, medium 0.36 -> 0.55, high 0.67 -> 0.64.
limits: Ablation set is 100 items with wide interval [37, 57]. Main-text AUROC for Sonnet-4.6 only in a figure.
agent_relevance: Rating changes little within one problem, so a gradual warmth curve over steps is not available from the model's words. Use code counts for within-run progress.

source: Wink (2026) Recovering from Misbehaviors in Coding Agents (authors not extracted)
finding: Production study of a coding agent: a classifier flags loops, drift and tool failures every 5 steps and injects a course correction. Reduces misbehaviour.
numbers: About 42,800 trajectories over 5 weeks: loops 5.21%, did-not-follow-instructions 15.95%, unrequested changes 6.62%, tool failures 14.02%; 29.2% overlapping total. Infinite loops: Sonnet 4.5 2.18%, Opus 4.5 3.59%. Single intervention recovered 90.93% (reasoning problems 94.29%); multiple 79.07% (reasoning 73.78%). Shadow mode misbehaviour 15.14% vs 18.61%, p=0.00003. 15-day A/B: tool failures -4.2%, tokens per session -5.3%, engineer interventions -4.2%, time -4.3% (p=0.073, not significant).
limits: Industry system; classifier is an LLM (precision bar 80%, recovery judge 85.71%). Of non-recovered cases 37% ignored the correction.
agent_relevance: Production proof that a periodic no-progress check pays a small but real gain. Loops are only about 5% of trajectories, so rule payoff is limited.

source: Cemri et al. (2025) Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail? (MAST)
finding: Large annotated trace study. Progress-monitoring failures are common: step repetition and not knowing when to stop.
numbers: 1,642 annotated traces, 7 frameworks, 14 failure modes. Step repetition 15.7%; unaware of termination conditions 12.4%; reasoning-action mismatch 13.2%; premature termination 6.2%; no or incomplete verification 8.2%; incorrect verification 9.1%. Human kappa 0.88; o1 judge kappa 0.77. Fix: added task-objective verification +15.6% success on ProgramDev (ChatDev); better role specs +9.4%.
limits: Only 7 open frameworks; percentages are shares of annotated failure modes, not of all runs. Read first 100,000 of 160,349 characters.
agent_relevance: Step repetition plus termination errors are 28% of annotated modes, which supports a count-based repeated-state rule and an explicit stop test.

source: Ma et al. (2019) Self-Monitoring Navigation Agent via Auxiliary Progress Estimation
finding: An older AI system built directly on a progress-monitoring idea: a learned module outputs how complete the instruction-following is (closeness to goal). It regularises training, backtracks, and re-ranks beam search.
numbers: Room-to-Room, validation-unseen success rate: baseline 0.27; co-grounding greedy 0.42; plus progress monitor 0.44; plus progress inference 0.46; beam search without monitor 0.49, with monitor 0.57; best row 0.58, SPL 0.52. Beam search alone +7% SR; with progress estimate +13%. Abstract: 8% absolute SR gain on unseen test.
limits: Navigation, not language reasoning; progress is a trained regression to ground-truth distance, which text problem solving lacks. Gain partly from beam search.
agent_relevance: Shows a graded progress score is most valuable as a ranking term among competing paths, not only as a stop signal.

source: Ma et al. (2019) The Regretful Agent: Heuristic-Aided Navigation through Progress Estimation
finding: A learned regret module decides when to go back to an earlier state, using a progress monitor as a search heuristic.
numbers: Abstract: 5% absolute success-rate gain on the R2R test server over greedy state-of-the-art, and 8% on success weighted by path length.
limits: Abstract only; absolute rates not stated in the page read. Regret module is a separate learned component.
agent_relevance: Backtracking trigger learned from progress: a template for a graded S6 rule.

source: Liu et al. (2025) Understanding R1-Zero-Like Training: A Critical Perspective
finding: The 'aha moment' of self-reflection already appears in base models and does not reliably help. Models do not use reflection as a progress check.
numbers: Nearly half of DeepSeek-R1-Zero responses with self-reflection are no more accurate than those without. Mean response length 7870.3 characters vs 880.7 for the base; incorrect 8206.1 vs correct 4965.4. Dr. GRPO 7B: AIME24 43.3, average 51.4.
limits: Reflection shares shown in figures only; incorrect answers may come from harder questions. Training-recipe paper, not a progress-monitoring test.
agent_relevance: Reflection words ('wait') are not evidence of progress. Do not read them as a signal.

source: From Aha Moments to Controllable Thinking, MERA (2025; authors not extracted)
finding: Splits reasoning from a control channel at 'wait' and 'alternatively' turning points; a trained control step decides continue or stop.
numbers: R1-Distill-Qwen 1.5B/7B/14B averaged over 5 benchmarks: 58.6 -> 62.4, 71.2 -> 76.0, 76.0 -> 79.8; tokens 8,379 -> 4,862, 7,488 -> 4,680, 7,316 -> 3,864. Ablation 7B: 71.2, SFT 73.2, SFT+GRPO 74.7, full 76.0. Out-of-domain Physics 34.1 -> 36.9.
limits: Control statements written by Llama-3.3-70B and scored by GPT-4o; training needed.
agent_relevance: Separating a monitor channel from the reasoning channel agrees with our code-decides, model-fills design.

source: Chen et al. (2025) Reasoning Models Don't Always Say What They Think
finding: Written reasoning often omits what drove the answer, so verbal statements of progress cannot be trusted as a record.
numbers: Hint acknowledged: Claude 3.7 Sonnet 25% overall, 20% on misalignment hints; DeepSeek R1 39% overall, 29%. About 44% (Claude) and 32% (R1) lower relative faithfulness on GPQA than MMLU. Reward hacks exploited in over 99% of examples but verbalised in under 2% in 5 of 6 settings.
limits: Tests hint use, not progress statements; per-hint rates only in a figure.
agent_relevance: Supports G10: judge progress from outputs, not narration.

source: CresOWLve: Benchmarking Creative Problem-Solving Over Real-World Knowledge (2026; authors not extracted)
finding: Insight-style puzzle benchmark: models often have the knowledge but fail to make the non-obvious link. More thinking effort helps.
numbers: 2,061 creative items, 5 levels, English and Russian; 14 models. Non-thinking models all under 30%. Best Gemini-3.1-Pro (high): English 51.29% exact match, 76.03% LLM judge; Russian 67.78% / 85.74%. Creative vs factual drop up to 17.21% (Mistral-Large-3); smallest -6.08%. 150 of 1,087 errors from Gemini-3-Flash analysed: top causes missing creative connection and clue misinterpretation.
limits: No human trial; the 100% human bound is implicit from the game. Does not measure progress monitoring.
agent_relevance: Closest insight-type LLM benchmark. Errors are failed restructuring, not lack of facts, so a progress trigger should prompt reframing, not retrieval.

source: Negative result: no LLM study of human progress-monitoring paradigms found (this agent, arXiv listing and API searches, 2026-11-01)
finding: I found no study that gives language models the human progress-monitoring tasks (anagram solvability judgments, feeling-of-warmth ratings, nine-dot or magic-trick insight problems) and compares their curves with the human gradual rise.
numbers: none found. arXiv title searches for 'insight problems language models' and 'feeling of knowing' returned only unrelated papers or Cao 2026; 'progress estimation agents' returned only the 2019 navigation papers and a 2026 report-agent paper.
limits: Absence of evidence under limited search: WebSearch quota ran out, Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex were rate-limited, arXiv returned 429 late in the run. A gap for a later pass.
agent_relevance: The human gradual-warmth finding has no direct LLM replication. Any graded trigger we build is design, not replication.

source: Synthesis (this agent) across Reflexion, ToT, DEER and the navigation progress monitor
finding: Hard count rules (Reflexion: 3 repeats or 30 actions) and graded scores (ToT sure/maybe/impossible; DEER confidence 0.95; navigation progress monitor) are both in use. No paper compares them head to head on the same tasks.
numbers: Hard rule: Reflexion +22% AlfWorld. Graded: ToT b=5 74% vs b=1 45% on Game of 24; navigation beam search with progress 0.57 vs 0.49 SR.
limits: No matched comparison exists; the numbers use different tasks and models.
agent_relevance: Our own logs must decide hard versus graded for S6. Test a count rule first and a graded rule second at equal tokens (G7).
